cards.t: Which of the following is an example of a sign?
cards.d: Patient's heart rate is elevated and irregular
w: Patient says the pain is sharp and comes and goes
cards.e: A sign is objective and can be observed or measured by someone else, such as a heart rate on a monitor. Dizziness and anxiety are symptoms the patient reports. Looks tired is also observable, but a measured heart rate is the clearest sign.
cards.qd: Patient's heart rate is elevated and irregular
qw: Patient reports dizziness that started after lunch
Patient reports feelings of anxiety about the test
Patient describes a sharp pain that comes and goes

cards.t: What is the condition called in which the body's systems are working together to maintain health and stability?
cards.e: Homeostasis is the balanced internal state the body keeps when its systems work together.

cards.t: Blood vessels and nerve endings are concentrated in which layer of the skin?
cards.e: The dermis holds blood vessels, nerve receptors, hair follicles, and oil glands. The epidermis is the outer layer.

cards.t: Which is one of the functions of muscles?
cards.d: Direct and coordinate the movements of the body
w: Supply oxygen and nutrients to the body
Carry sensory messages to the brain
cards.e: On the sheet, the key is 'direct and coordinate the movements of the body'. Muscles also produce heat, which is a real muscle function, but it was not the keyed answer.
cards.qd: Direct and coordinate the movements of the body
qw: Supply oxygen and nutrients to the blood
Rid the body of wastes and extra fluid
Carry sensory messages up to the brain

cards.t: How does the nervous system send messages to the brain?
cards.d: Through neurons, from receptors throughout the body and then through the spinal cord
w: Through the blood that flows to the head
Through a network of special vessels carrying neuron-filled fluid
From the right hemisphere of the cerebrum to the left hemisphere
cards.e: Sensory neurons carry signals from receptors to the spinal cord, which relays them up to the brain.
cards.qd: Through neurons, from receptors throughout the body, then through the spinal cord
qw: Through the blood that flows from the heart to the head, then back down through the veins to the body.
Through special vessels that carry neuron-filled fluid up the spine and across to the brain stem.
From the right cerebral hemisphere across to the left hemisphere, then down through the cerebellum.

cards.t: Which of the following is part of the peripheral nervous system?
cards.e: The brainstem, spinal cord, and cerebral cortex make up the central nervous system. The peripheral nervous system is everything outside the brain and spinal cord.
cards.qd: The eyes, along with the nerves that serve them
qw: The spinal cord, which runs down the back
The cerebral cortex, the outer layer of the brain

cards.t: Which movement is peristalsis?
cards.d: The process that moves food through the gastrointestinal system
w: The process that transmits information from the sense organs to the brain
The process that causes blood to clot
The process that secretes hormones that regulate body processes
cards.e: Peristalsis is rhythmic muscle contraction that moves food along the digestive tract.
cards.qd: The process that moves food through the gastrointestinal system
qw: The process that moves information from the sense organs to the brain
The process that causes blood to clot after an injury
The process that secretes hormones to regulate body processes

cards.t: Which gland is also known as the master gland?
cards.e: The pituitary gland controls other endocrine glands through its hormones, which is why it is called the master gland.

cards.t: Progesterone is a hormone associated with which system?
w: Regulation of calcium levels in the blood
Movement of glucose from the blood into the cells of the body
cards.e: Progesterone prepares and maintains the uterus during the menstrual cycle and pregnancy.
qw: Regulation of calcium levels in the blood
Movement of glucose from the blood into the cells

cards.t: Which describes a type of acquired immunity?
cards.d: A person is exposed to influenza but does not become ill because he had received an influenza vaccine three weeks before
w: A person is exposed to influenza but does not become ill because he is always very careful about washing hands
An infant does not become sick with influenza, despite being too young to receive the vaccine, because everyone around him has received it
A person is exposed to influenza but does not become ill because he was wearing a mask at the time
cards.e: Vaccination produces acquired (adaptive) immunity: the body builds memory against the germ before exposure.
cards.qd: A person is exposed to influenza but does not become ill because he had received an influenza vaccine three weeks before
qw: A person is exposed to influenza but does not become ill because he is always very careful about washing hands
An infant does not become sick with influenza, despite being too young to receive the vaccine, because everyone around him has received it
A person is exposed to influenza but does not become ill because he was wearing a mask at the time

cards.t: Lymph is a fluid that circulates through which means?
w: Only in times of strong immune system response
cards.e: Lymph has no pump of its own. Skeletal muscle movement, breathing, and massage push it through one-way lymph vessels.
qw: The pumping of the heart and the arteries
The spinal column and the nerves that run through it
Only during a strong immune response to infection

cards.t: Which term describes the condition in which all of the body's systems are balanced and working together to maintain internal stability?
cards.e: Homeostasis is the state of balance that the body's systems maintain together.

cards.t: Which term means the physical and chemical processes by which substances are broken down or transformed into energy or products for use by the body?
cards.e: Metabolism covers all the chemical reactions that turn food and other substances into energy and useful products.

cards.t: Which term means objective information about a person's health that can be observed or measured?
cards.e: Signs are objective. A clinician can see, hear, or measure them, such as fever or a rash.

cards.t: Which term means subjective information about a person's health, reported only by the patient?
cards.e: Symptoms are subjective. Only the patient can feel them, such as pain, dizziness, or nausea.

cards.t: Which term means a structural unit in the human body that performs a specific function?
cards.e: An organ is made of several tissues working together to perform a specific function, such as the heart.

cards.t: Which term means a group of cells that perform a similar task?
cards.e: Tissue is a group of similar cells that work together, such as muscle or nerve tissue.

cards.t: Which term means the basic structural unit of the body?
cards.e: The cell is the smallest living unit of the body, and all tissues and organs are built from cells.

cards.t: Which anatomical term means the front of the body or body part?
cards.e: Anterior, or ventral, means toward the front of the body.

cards.t: Which anatomical term means farther away from the torso?
cards.e: Distal means farther from the trunk. The hand is distal to the shoulder.

cards.t: Which anatomical term means toward the midline of the body?
cards.e: Medial means toward the midline. The chest is medial to the arm.

cards.t: Which anatomical term means away from the head?
cards.e: Inferior means lower, away from the head. The feet are inferior to the hips.

cards.t: Which anatomical term means the back of the body or body part?
cards.e: Posterior, or dorsal, means toward the back of the body.

cards.t: Which anatomical term means to the side, away from the midline of the body?
cards.e: Lateral means away from the midline. The ear is lateral to the head's center.

cards.t: Which anatomical term means toward the head?
cards.e: Superior means higher, toward the head. The nose is superior to the mouth.

cards.t: Which anatomical term means closer to the torso?
cards.e: Proximal means nearer to the trunk or to the point where a structure attaches. It is the opposite of distal.

cards.t: What is the largest organ and system in the body?
cards.e: The integumentary system is the skin with its hair, nails, and glands. It is the largest organ system.
qw: The liver and its bile system

cards.t: What does the skin prevent from reaching the internal organs?
cards.e: Intact skin is a physical barrier that keeps germs and harmful substances out of the body.
qw: Oxygen, nutrients, and the body's own blood cells
Blood cells and other body fluids
Hormones and the chemicals they carry

cards.t: Skin also prevents the loss of too much what, which is essential to life?
cards.e: The skin's outer layer slows water loss, and keeping enough water in the body is essential to life.
cards.qd: Water and moisture from the body
qw: Blood and plasma from the vessels

cards.t: The skin is also a sensory what that feels heat, cold, pain, touch, and pressure?
cards.e: Nerve receptors in the skin detect heat, cold, pain, touch, and pressure.

cards.t: What do blood vessels do when the outside temperature is too high?
cards.e: Widening lets more blood reach the skin, so heat can leave the body.

cards.t: What do blood vessels do when the outside temperature is too cold?
cards.e: Narrowing reduces blood flow to the skin and keeps heat in the body's core.

cards.t: Capillaries, the smallest what in the body, are located in which layer of skin?
cards.e: Capillaries are the smallest blood vessels, and they sit in the dermis, the inner layer of skin.

cards.t: Which layer of skin is the inner layer, where the capillaries are located?
cards.e: The dermis is the inner, middle layer of skin, containing blood vessels, nerves, and hair follicles.

cards.t: Which layer of skin has no blood vessels and only a few nerve endings?
cards.e: The epidermis is the outer layer. It has no blood vessels and receives nutrients from the dermis below.

cards.t: Blood tests for IgE, a type of what, may be part of an allergy diagnosis?
cards.e: IgE is an antibody the immune system makes during allergic reactions.

cards.t: A complete blood count may be ordered because allergies can increase the number of which type of blood cell?
cards.d: Eosinophils (a type of white blood cell)
cards.e: Allergies can raise the eosinophil count, a type of white blood cell, so a CBC can show it.
cards.qd: Eosinophils (a type of white blood cell)
qw: Neutrophils (a type of white blood cell)

cards.t: Which is a tissue of the body that helps shape it?
cards.d: Muscles, bones, ligaments, tendons, and cartilage
cards.e: The body's shape comes from the musculoskeletal structures: muscles, bones, ligaments, tendons, and cartilage.
cards.s: MedlinePlus: The structure of a joint
cards.qd: Muscles, bones, ligaments, tendons, and cartilage
qw: Skin, fat, and the connective tissue beneath it
The heart, lungs, and the digestive organs
Blood vessels, nerves, and the glands they serve

cards.t: How many bones does an adult human body have?
cards.e: An adult has 206 bones. The sheet's 215 is marked false.
cards.s: MedlinePlus: The structure of a joint

cards.t: What do bones do for the body's organs?
cards.e: Bones form a hard shell that shields the organs inside, such as the skull around the brain.
cards.s: MedlinePlus: The structure of a joint
cards.qd: Protect them from injury and shield them from blows
qw: Pump blood through them and out to the lungs
Digest the food stored in them each day
Filter the blood through tiny vessels inside them

cards.t: What is the place where two bones meet called?
cards.e: Two bones meet at a joint, and ligaments hold the bones together there.
cards.s: MedlinePlus: The structure of a joint

cards.t: What allows movement of body parts?
cards.e: Muscles contract and pull on bones through tendons, which produces movement.

cards.t: Which statement about muscle control is correct?
cards.d: Not all muscles are voluntary; heart and smooth muscle work without conscious control
w: All muscles move only when a person wants them to
Muscles cannot be controlled by the nervous system
cards.e: Skeletal muscle is voluntary. Cardiac and smooth muscle are involuntary.
cards.qd: Not all muscles are voluntary; heart and smooth muscle work without conscious control
qw: All muscles move only when a person consciously chooses to move them
Only heart muscle is voluntary, and skeletal muscle moves on its own
Muscles cannot be controlled by the nervous system, so they move on their own

cards.t: What do muscles produce for the body?
cards.e: Muscle activity produces heat, which helps keep the body warm.
qw: Blood cells and platelets for clotting

cards.t: In which way does a hinge joint move?
cards.d: In one plane, like the elbow or knee
w: Only in a circle around its center
cards.e: A hinge joint bends and straightens in one plane. The elbow and knee are hinge joints.
cards.s: MedlinePlus: The structure of a joint
cards.qd: In one plane, like the elbow or knee
qw: In all directions, like a ball and socket
Only in a circle around its center
It does not move, to keep the joint stable

cards.t: Do the tissues of bones need oxygen and nutrients?
cards.d: Yes, bone tissue is living and needs oxygen and nutrients
w: No, bones are hard and do not need oxygen or nutrients
cards.e: Bone is living tissue with its own blood supply. The statement that bones need no oxygen is false.
cards.s: MedlinePlus: The structure of a joint
cards.qd: Yes, bone tissue is living and needs oxygen and nutrients
qw: No, bones are hard and do not need oxygen or nutrients
Only the outer covering needs oxygen
Only the joints need oxygen and nutrients

cards.t: What attaches skeletal muscles to bones?
cards.e: Tendons are fibrous tissue that attach skeletal muscle to bone so the bone can move.

cards.t: Which test can help diagnose arthritis?
cards.e: Blood tests for specific antibodies, such as rheumatoid factor, can help diagnose arthritis.
qw: A urine test for certain proteins
A sweat test for salt levels

cards.t: Which describes the nervous system?
w: Gives the body shape and structure
Is the largest organ in the body
Pumps blood through the blood vessels to the cells
cards.e: The nervous system controls and coordinates body functions through electrical and chemical signals.
qw: Pumps blood through vessels to every cell
Gives the skeleton its shape and strength
Stores fat and regulates body heat

cards.t: What are the two main parts of the nervous system?
cards.d: The central nervous system and peripheral nervous system
w: The cardiovascular system and integumentary system
cards.e: The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord. The peripheral nervous system is the nerves outside them.
cards.qd: The central nervous system and peripheral nervous system
qw: The cardiovascular system and integumentary system
The sensory system and the endocrine system
The neurons and receptors of the body

cards.t: What is the basic unit of the nervous system, also called a nerve cell?
cards.e: A neuron is the nerve cell. It receives and sends electrical signals.

cards.t: The peripheral nervous system deals with the outer part of the body through the what?
cards.e: The peripheral nervous system is made of nerves that reach the outer parts of the body.

cards.t: What cushions the brain and spinal cord against injury?
cards.e: Cerebrospinal fluid surrounds and cushions the brain and spinal cord.
qw: Lymph fluid from the lymph nodes

cards.t: Which part of the brain controls thinking, speech, and voluntary muscles?
cards.e: The cerebral cortex is the outer layer of the cerebrum and controls thinking, speech, and voluntary movement.

cards.t: The left hemisphere of the brain controls which side of the body?
cards.d: The right side of the body
w: The left side of the body
cards.e: Each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.
cards.qd: The right side of the body
qw: The left side of the body

cards.t: The brainstem controls which functions?
cards.e: The brainstem controls automatic functions such as breathing, heart rate, and swallowing.
qw: Memory and learning of new skills

cards.t: The nerve pathways in the spinal cord conduct messages between which parts?
cards.e: Spinal cord nerve pathways carry messages between the brain and the rest of the body.

cards.t: The central nervous system is made up of which organs?
cards.e: The brain and spinal cord together make up the central nervous system.
qw: The skull and the vertebral column

cards.t: List the five sense organs of the body.
cards.d: Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin
w: Heart, lungs, liver, kidneys, and skin
Brain, spinal cord, nerves, eyes, and ears
Stomach, intestines, bladder, skin, and nose
cards.e: The five senses are sight (eyes), hearing and balance (ears), smell (nose), taste (tongue), and touch (skin).
cards.qd: Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin
qw: Heart, lungs, liver, kidneys, and skin
Brain, spinal cord, nerves, eyes, and ears
Stomach, intestines, bladder, skin, and nose

cards.t: Which part of the eye contains cells that respond to light and send a message to the brain so a person can see?
cards.e: The retina contains light-sensitive cells that send signals through the optic nerve to the brain.

cards.t: What are the three parts of the ear?
cards.d: Outer ear, middle ear, and inner ear
cards.e: The outer ear collects sound, the middle ear carries it through the ossicles, and the inner ear holds the hearing and balance organs.
cards.qd: Outer ear, middle ear, and inner ear
qw: Pinna, cochlea, and eardrum, each with its own fluid
Cornea, lens, and the iris, with the retina behind
Brain, nerve, and eardrum, linked by the ossicles

cards.t: Why may a provider order blood tests when diagnosing a possible stroke or a nervous system disorder such as Parkinson's disease?
cards.d: To look for clues such as infection, blood sugar problems, and clotting problems, and to rule out other causes
w: To measure the size of the brain
To confirm Parkinson's disease by itself
To check the strength of the spinal nerves
cards.e: No single blood test diagnoses stroke or Parkinson's. Tests help find causes and rule out others that can look similar.
cards.qd: To look for infection, blood sugar problems, or clotting problems, and rule out other causes
qw: To measure the size of the brain and the blood flow inside it
To confirm Parkinson's disease by itself, since no other tests are needed for the diagnosis
To check how strong the spinal nerves are when the patient moves

cards.t: Where does respiration (gas exchange) occur?
cards.e: Gas exchange happens in the lungs' alveoli, where oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.

cards.t: What is expiration?
cards.e: Expiration is breathing out. Inspiration is breathing in.

cards.t: What does the respiratory system do?
cards.d: Brings oxygen into the body and eliminates carbon dioxide
cards.e: The respiratory system takes in oxygen and removes carbon dioxide.
cards.qd: Brings oxygen into the body and eliminates carbon dioxide
qw: Pumps blood to every cell and then returns it to the heart
Digests food and absorbs nutrients into the bloodstream
Filters waste from the blood and stores it in the bladder

cards.t: Which structure is also called the windpipe?
cards.e: The larynx is the voice box. The trachea, or windpipe, runs from the larynx to the bronchi.

cards.t: Where are oxygen and carbon dioxide exchanged?
cards.d: Between the alveoli and the capillaries
w: Between the bronchi and the larynx
Between the pleura and the trachea
Between the veins and the arteries
cards.e: Gas exchange happens across the thin walls shared by the alveoli and the capillaries.
cards.qd: Between the alveoli and the capillaries
qw: Between the bronchi and the larynx
Between the pleura and the trachea
Between the veins and the arteries

cards.t: The pleura is a two-layered membrane that does what?
cards.e: The pleura is a two-layered membrane that wraps the lungs and lines the chest cavity.

cards.t: Which structure divides into the right and left bronchi?
cards.e: The trachea divides into the right and left main bronchi. The pharynx is the throat, above the trachea.

cards.t: Which vessel carries oxygen-saturated blood to the left side of the heart?
cards.e: The pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

cards.t: What is located between the layers of the pleura?
w: Special tissue that protects the respiratory system from pathogens
cards.e: A thin layer of pleural fluid lets the two pleural layers glide during breathing.
qw: Air trapped between the two layers

cards.t: In adult patients, blood gas testing is usually performed on blood from which vessels?
cards.e: Arterial blood gas tests use arterial blood, which shows how well the lungs are moving oxygen and carbon dioxide.

cards.t: What is one function of the urinary system?
cards.d: Filtering wastes and excess water from the blood
cards.e: The urinary system filters blood, removes wastes, and balances water and salts. It also helps control blood pressure.
cards.qd: Filtering wastes and excess water from the blood
qw: Pumping blood through the heart and lungs
Breaking down food into nutrients for cells
Carrying air to the alveoli in the lungs

cards.t: What are the parts of the urinary system?
cards.d: Kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, and urethra
w: Brain, spinal cord, nerves, and retina
cards.e: Kidneys filter blood, ureters carry urine, the bladder stores it, and the urethra releases it.
cards.qd: Kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, and urethra
qw: Brain, spinal cord, nerves, and retina

cards.t: Where are waste products and excess water filtered from the blood?
cards.e: The kidneys filter the blood and make urine from wastes and excess water.

cards.t: What path does urine follow from the kidneys to leave the body?
cards.e: Urine travels from the kidneys through the ureters to the bladder, then out through the urethra.

cards.t: What is the name of the series of blood tests that may be ordered to evaluate kidney health?
cards.e: A renal function panel measures waste products such as creatinine and BUN to check how well the kidneys work.
qw: Liver function panel (hepatic panel) with bilirubin
Arterial blood gas (ABG) panel for pH and oxygen

cards.t: What task related to the diagnosis of urinary tract infection may be assigned to a phlebotomy technician?
w: Reading the urine culture under a microscope
cards.e: Collecting a clean urine specimen for testing is a task that can be assigned to a phlebotomy technician.
qw: Ordering a urine culture for the lab
Reading the ultrasound of the kidney

cards.t: Process of expelling wastes (made up of the waste products of food and fluids) that are not absorbed into the cells?
cards.e: Defecation expels the undigested and unabsorbed waste from the rectum.

cards.t: Which term describes involuntary contractions that move food into the stomach from the esophagus?
cards.e: Peristalsis is the wave-like muscle movement that pushes food down the digestive tract.
qw: Digestion (breakdown of food into smaller pieces)
Absorption (uptake of nutrients into the blood)

cards.t: What is the transfer of nutrients from the intestines to the cells called?
cards.e: Absorption moves nutrients across the intestinal wall into the blood and lymph.

cards.t: What is the semisolid material made up of water, solid waste, bacteria, and mucus that passes through the rectum and out of the body?
cards.e: Feces are the solid waste the large intestine forms and eliminates.

cards.t: What is the process of preparing food physically and chemically so that it can be absorbed into the cells?
cards.e: Digestion breaks food down mechanically and chemically into nutrients the cells can absorb.

cards.t: What is the semiliquid substance created by breaking down food in the stomach?
cards.e: Chyme is the partly digested food mixture that leaves the stomach for the small intestine.

cards.t: Which muscular pouch is located in the upper left part of the abdominal cavity?
cards.e: The stomach is a muscular pouch in the upper left abdomen where food is churned and mixed.

cards.t: What parts and organs of the body are considered accessories to digestion?
cards.d: Teeth, tongue, salivary glands, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas
cards.e: The accessory organs help digestion without being part of the digestive tube itself.
cards.qd: Teeth, tongue, salivary glands, liver, and pancreas
qw: Lungs, heart, kidneys, spleen, bladder, and the uterus
Brain, spinal cord, nerves, eyes, ears, and the nose
Skin, hair, nails, sweat glands, the thyroid, and the spleen

cards.t: Which CLIA-waived test related to the digestive system may be performed by a phlebotomy technician or other certified healthcare worker?
cards.e: The fecal occult blood test checks stool for hidden blood and is CLIA-waived.
cards.s: FDA: CLIA — Tests Waived by FDA
qw: Liver biopsy of the portal tissue

cards.t: What part of the body does a hepatic function panel relate to?
cards.e: A hepatic (liver) function panel measures enzymes and bilirubin that show how the liver is working.

cards.t: The endocrine system is made up of what in different areas of the body?
cards.e: Endocrine glands release hormones directly into the blood, and they are spread across the body.

cards.t: What are chemical substances created by the body that control numerous body functions?
cards.e: Hormones are chemical messengers that control many body functions.

cards.t: Which three hormones are secreted by the pituitary gland?
cards.d: Growth hormone, prolactin, and adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)
cards.e: The pituitary releases growth hormone, prolactin, and ACTH, among others. The wrong options come from other glands.
cards.qd: Growth hormone, prolactin, and adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)
qw: Insulin, glucagon, and thyroxine from the pancreas
Adrenaline, estrogen, and testosterone from the gonads
Melatonin, cortisol, and aldosterone from the adrenal glands

cards.t: Where is the thyroid gland located, and what does its hormone regulate?
cards.d: In the neck; the body's metabolic rate
cards.e: The thyroid sits in the neck and its hormones set the rate of metabolism.
cards.qd: In the neck; the body's metabolic rate
qw: In the neck; blood calcium levels
In the abdomen; the body's metabolic rate
In the chest; the body's heart rate

cards.t: The parathyroid glands secrete a hormone that regulates the body's use of what?
cards.e: Parathyroid hormone raises blood calcium levels when they are low.
cards.qd: Calcium in the blood and bones
qw: Glucose in the blood and cells
Sodium and potassium in body fluids

cards.t: Insulin, a hormone that moves glucose (natural sugar) from the blood into cells for energy, is secreted by which gland?
cards.e: Insulin is made by the pancreas, and it lowers blood glucose by moving it into cells.

cards.t: During which situations does adrenaline regulate muscle power, heart rate, blood pressure, and energy levels?
cards.e: Adrenaline prepares the body for fight or flight during stress or emergencies.
qw: Deep sleep and quiet rest periods during the night
Eating a large meal slowly with family members
Routine daily tasks and paperwork at the office

cards.t: Patients with diabetes may test their own blood to determine how much of which substance is present?
cards.e: Blood glucose monitoring shows how much sugar is in the blood so treatment can be adjusted.

cards.t: Glucose challenge tests are commonly performed during which period to check for gestational diabetes?
cards.e: CDC describes gestational diabetes screening during pregnancy, usually between 24 and 28 weeks.

cards.t: The male and female sex glands are the what?
cards.e: The gonads are the testes in males and the ovaries in females.

cards.t: The hormone needed for male reproductive organs to function properly is what?
cards.e: Testosterone is the main male sex hormone that supports the male reproductive organs.

cards.t: What are the gonads in females called?
cards.e: The ovaries are the female gonads. They produce eggs and make estrogen and progesterone.

cards.t: The female reproductive cycle is maintained by which hormones?
cards.e: Estrogen and progesterone rise and fall through the cycle to control the uterine lining.

cards.t: Pregnancy tests detect the presence of which hormone?
cards.e: hCG is made by the placenta after implantation and shows up in urine and blood.

cards.t: The reproductive system allows humans to do what?
cards.e: The reproductive system makes it possible to create new human life.
qw: Coordinate movement of the limbs and the spine
Process and store long-term memories in the brain
Fight infections in the blood and lymph system

cards.t: The immune system protects the body from disease-causing bacteria, viruses, and what else?
cards.e: The immune system defends against bacteria, viruses, and other microorganisms that cause disease.

cards.t: Which type of immunity protects the body from disease in general?
cards.e: Innate immunity is the protection a person is born with, such as skin and white blood cells.

cards.t: Which type of immunity protects against a disease that is invading the body at a given time?
cards.e: Acquired immunity targets a specific germ and builds memory after infection or vaccination.

cards.t: The lymphatic system removes excess what and waste products from the tissues?
cards.e: The lymphatic system drains excess tissue fluid and returns it to the blood.

cards.t: What is the clear yellowish fluid that carries disease-fighting cells?
cards.e: Lymph is the fluid of the lymphatic system and carries white blood cells.

cards.t: What are the disease-fighting cells carried in lymph called?
cards.e: Lymphocytes are white blood cells that carry out immune responses.

cards.t: List three ways the body protects itself against disease in general.
cards.d: Skin and mucous membranes as barriers, inflammation and fever, and white blood cells that attack invaders
cards.e: Physical barriers, chemical barriers, inflammation, and white blood cells all defend the body.
cards.qd: Skin and mucous membranes as barriers, inflammation and fever, and white blood cells
qw: Taking antibiotics daily, avoiding all crowds, and drinking extra water every single day
Avoiding all contact with germs and staying indoors all week during cold and flu season
Making more red blood cells and platelets in the marrow every day to fight infection

cards.t: What are two ways a person can gain acquired immunity?
cards.d: By having the disease (natural infection) and by vaccination (artificial)
w: Eating a balanced diet and sleeping well
cards.e: Natural acquired immunity comes from infection; artificial acquired immunity comes from vaccines.
cards.qd: By having the disease (natural infection) and by vaccination (artificial)
qw: Eating a balanced diet and getting enough sleep every single night of the week
Exercise, fresh air, and a daily walk outside in the neighborhood each morning
Inheriting it from parents, with no other way to gain it at any point in life

cards.t: Why is muscle activity important to the function of the lymphatic system?
cards.d: Lymph has no pump, so muscle movement and breathing squeeze lymph vessels and push lymph toward the heart
w: It makes lymph nodes produce antibodies
It pumps lymph into the arteries
cards.e: Lymph vessels have one-way valves, so muscle and breathing movement moves lymph toward the heart.
cards.qd: Lymph has no pump, so muscle movement and breathing squeeze lymph toward the heart
qw: It makes lymph nodes produce more antibodies each hour during an active infection
It pumps lymph directly into the arteries of the legs to speed circulation
It keeps lymph from clotting inside the vessels and drains the blood in the body

cards.t: Which term means a wall that divides the heart into left and right sides?
cards.e: The septum is the muscular wall between the heart's left and right sides.

cards.t: Which chambers of the heart receive blood returning to the heart?
cards.e: The atria are the upper chambers that receive blood coming into the heart.

cards.t: What does the term ventricular describe?
cards.d: Relating to the ventricles, the lower chambers that pump blood out of the heart
w: Relating to the veins that return blood
cards.e: Ventricular means of the ventricles, which pump blood into the arteries.
cards.qd: Relating to the ventricles, the lower chambers that pump blood out
qw: Relating to the atria, the upper chambers that receive blood
Relating to the veins that return blood to the heart
Relating to the blood cells made in the bone marrow

cards.t: What is the heart's natural pacemaker, which starts each heartbeat?
cards.e: The SA node in the right atrium starts each electrical impulse, so it sets the heart rate.

cards.t: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart in the heart worksheet?
cards.e: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Veins carry blood back toward it.

cards.t: What are Purkinje fibers?
cards.d: Specialized fibers in the ventricle walls that conduct electrical impulses so the ventricles contract
w: Fibers that carry oxygen to the lungs
Valves that stop backflow of blood
cards.e: Purkinje fibers spread the heart's electrical impulses through the ventricles.
cards.qd: Specialized fibers in the ventricle walls that conduct electrical impulses
qw: Fibers that carry oxygen from the lungs to the brain and muscles of the arm
Cells in the bone marrow that make red blood cells for the body
Valves that stop backflow of blood into the atria during each beat

cards.t: What does it mean to palpate a vein?
cards.d: To examine it by touch with the fingers
w: To look at it with a magnifying light
To measure its diameter with a ruler
To listen to it with a stethoscope
cards.e: Palpation means feeling with the fingertips. Vein palpation is part of selecting a site for a blood draw.
cards.qd: To examine it by touch with the fingers
qw: To look at it with a magnifying light
To measure its diameter with a ruler
To listen to it with a stethoscope

cards.t: What is the liquid portion of blood called?
cards.e: Plasma is the straw-colored liquid that carries cells and proteins.

cards.t: What are erythrocytes?
cards.d: Red blood cells that carry oxygen
w: White blood cells that fight infection
cards.e: Erythrocytes are red blood cells. Hemoglobin inside them carries oxygen.
cards.qd: Red blood cells that carry oxygen
qw: White blood cells that fight infection

cards.t: What are leukocytes?
cards.d: White blood cells that defend the body
w: Red blood cells that carry oxygen
cards.e: Leukocytes are white blood cells, and they defend the body against infection.
cards.qd: White blood cells that defend the body
qw: Red blood cells that carry oxygen

cards.t: What are thrombocytes?
cards.d: Platelets, cell fragments that help blood clot
w: White blood cells that make antibodies
cards.e: Thrombocytes are platelets. They gather at an injury and start the clot.
cards.qd: Platelets, cell fragments that help blood clot
qw: Red blood cells that carry oxygen to the tissues
White blood cells that make antibodies
Plasma proteins that carry hormones and nutrients

cards.t: What are lymphocytes?
cards.d: A type of white blood cell that drives immune responses (B and T cells)
cards.e: Lymphocytes include B and T cells, which produce targeted immune responses.
cards.qd: A type of white blood cell that drives immune responses (B and T cells)
qw: Red blood cells that carry oxygen to the body's tissues and organs
Platelets that help the blood clot after an injury to a vessel
Plasma proteins that carry hormones, nutrients, and waste products

cards.t: What are antigens?
cards.d: Substances on cell surfaces, such as red cell proteins, that the immune system recognizes as foreign
cards.e: Antigens trigger antibody production. Blood types depend on red cell antigens.
cards.qd: Substances, such as red cell proteins, that the immune system recognizes as foreign
qw: Antibodies made by plasma cells to fight infection and recognize germs in the blood
Enzymes that break down clots after the healing of a wound and restore normal flow
Hormones that regulate blood pressure, heart rate, and fluid balance in the body

cards.t: What does Rh-positive mean?
cards.d: Red blood cells have the Rh (D) antigen
w: Red blood cells lack the Rh antigen
cards.e: Rh-positive blood has the Rh antigen on its red cells.
cards.qd: Red blood cells have the Rh (D) antigen
qw: Red blood cells lack the Rh (D) antigen entirely
Blood has no antibodies against any red cells
Blood cannot be safely transfused to any patient

cards.t: What is thrombosis?
cards.d: Formation of a blood clot inside a blood vessel that can block blood flow
cards.e: Thrombosis is an abnormal clot inside a vessel, which can cause heart attack, stroke, or DVT.
cards.qd: Formation of a blood clot inside a blood vessel that can block blood flow
qw: Bleeding that will not stop after a cut or minor injury to the skin
Breakdown of a clot by the body's own enzymes over several days
A low platelet count caused by a disorder of the bone marrow

cards.t: What is hemostasis?
cards.d: The process that stops bleeding after an injury
cards.e: Hemostasis stops bleeding through vessel constriction, platelet plugs, and clotting.
cards.qd: The process that stops bleeding after an injury
qw: Breakdown of clots after the wound has healed
A drop in blood sugar after a meal
The normal range of blood pressure at rest

cards.t: What is thrombin?
cards.d: An enzyme that converts fibrinogen into fibrin to form a clot
w: A plasma protein that carries oxygen
A hormone that narrows blood vessels
cards.e: Thrombin is the clotting enzyme that makes fibrin from fibrinogen.
cards.qd: An enzyme that converts fibrinogen into fibrin to form a clot
qw: A plasma protein that carries oxygen to the tissues of the body
A type of platelet that releases clotting signals at a wound
A hormone that narrows blood vessels after an injury to the body

cards.t: What is fibrinogen?
cards.d: A plasma protein that is converted into fibrin during clotting
w: A type of white blood cell
A hormone made by the pancreas
cards.e: Fibrinogen is a plasma protein. Thrombin turns it into fibrin, the clot's mesh.
cards.qd: A plasma protein that is converted into fibrin during clotting
qw: A red blood cell pigment that carries oxygen to the tissues
A type of white blood cell that fights germs in the blood
A hormone made by the pancreas to lower blood sugar

cards.t: What is hemophilia?
cards.d: An inherited bleeding disorder caused by a shortage of a clotting factor
w: An infection of the blood vessels
A blood type that lacks Rh factor
cards.e: Hemophilia is inherited. It causes bleeding because a clotting factor is missing or does not work.
cards.qd: An inherited bleeding disorder caused by a shortage of a clotting factor
qw: An infection of the blood vessels that causes bleeding and bruising
A form of blood cancer that causes the blood to clot too easily
A blood type that lacks the Rh factor and cannot be transfused

cards.t: What is a thrombus?
cards.d: A blood clot that stays attached to a vessel wall
w: A clot that travels through the blood
A deposit of fat in the arteries
cards.e: A thrombus forms and stays in place. A clot that travels is an embolus.
cards.qd: A blood clot that stays attached to a vessel wall
qw: A clot that travels through the blood to the lungs
A deposit of fat that builds up inside the arteries
A type of antibody made in the bone marrow

cards.t: What is a pulmonary embolism?
cards.d: A blockage in the lung's arteries, usually by a clot that traveled from another part of the body
w: A clot in a vein of the arm
cards.e: A pulmonary embolism blocks blood flow to the lungs. The clot often starts in a leg vein.
cards.qd: A blockage in the lung's arteries, usually from a clot that traveled from the body
qw: A clot in a vein of the arm that stays in place and grows slowly over many weeks
A collapse of the alveoli from a lack of surfactant in the lung tissue
Inflammation of the pleura after a chest infection or a blunt injury to the chest

cards.t: The circulatory system is also known as the what?
cards.e: The circulatory system and the cardiovascular system are the same system.

cards.t: The heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs and oxygenated blood to where?
w: The extremities and heart muscle only
cards.e: The right heart sends deoxygenated blood to the lungs. The left heart sends oxygenated blood to the entire body.
cards.qd: The entire body through the aorta
qw: The limbs and the brain only
The extremities and the heart muscle

cards.t: The valves of the heart function to do what?
cards.d: Keep blood flowing in the correct direction through the heart
w: Protect the arteries from extreme pressure
Send electrical signals that cause the heart to contract
Measure the amount of blood flowing through the heart
cards.e: One-way valves keep blood moving forward through the heart.
cards.qd: Keep blood flowing in the correct direction through the heart
qw: Protect the arteries from extreme pressure
Send electrical signals that cause the heart to contract
Measure the amount of blood flowing through the heart

cards.t: Which is the main pacemaker of the heart?
cards.e: The sinoatrial node is the heart's main pacemaker.

cards.t: The smallest blood vessels are called what?
cards.e: Capillaries are the smallest vessels, and they connect arterioles to venules.

cards.t: Which blood vessels almost always carry oxygenated blood?
cards.e: Arteries carry oxygenated blood from the heart. The pulmonary arteries are an exception.

cards.t: Which layer in blood vessels is made up mostly of muscle tissue and elastic fibers?
cards.e: The tunica media is the middle layer of a vessel wall and controls its diameter.

cards.t: Which blood vessel type typically holds about 70 percent of the body's blood?
cards.e: Veins hold most of the blood volume at rest.
cards.qd: The veins, which hold most of the blood at rest
qw: The arteries, which carry blood under high pressure
The chambers of the heart, which pump all blood
The capillaries, which exchange gases with tissue

cards.t: Which set of words best describes how a healthy vein feels when palpated?
cards.e: A healthy vein is elastic and springy. A firm, rope-like vein can signal a problem.

cards.t: The formed elements of blood make up what part of the blood volume?
cards.e: Formed elements, mainly red cells, make up about 45 percent of blood volume.
cards.qd: A bit less than one-half of the blood volume
qw: About one-third of the blood volume
A bit more than one-half of the blood volume
About two-thirds of the blood volume

cards.t: The liquid portion of blood is what?
cards.d: A combination of water and dissolved substances
w: Entirely made of oxygen in oxygenated blood and carbon dioxide in deoxygenated blood
What gives blood its red color
cards.e: Plasma is mostly water with dissolved proteins, electrolytes, and nutrients.
cards.qd: A combination of water and dissolved substances
qw: Mostly made of red blood cells in suspension
Entirely made of oxygen and carbon dioxide gas
The pigment that gives blood its red color

cards.t: Which type of blood cell contains hemoglobin?
cards.e: Hemoglobin is the oxygen-carrying protein inside red blood cells.

cards.t: Which part of the body is associated with the creation of blood cells?
cards.e: Blood cells are made in the red bone marrow.

cards.t: What can be said about a person with blood type A negative?
cards.d: They have type A antigens, anti-B antibodies, and no Rh factor
w: They have type B antigens, anti-A antibodies, and no Rh factor
They have type A antigens, anti-B antibodies, and Rh factor
They will naturally possess anti-Rh antibodies
cards.e: Type A has A antigens and anti-B antibodies. Negative means no Rh (D) antigen.
cards.qd: They have type A antigens, anti-B antibodies, and no Rh factor
qw: They have type B antigens, anti-A antibodies, and no Rh factor
They have type A antigens, anti-B antibodies, and Rh factor
They will naturally possess anti-Rh antibodies, which can cause a reaction

cards.t: Who could safely donate blood for a patient with blood type AB negative?
cards.e: O negative is the universal red cell donor type, and it has no Rh antigen, so it is safe for Rh-negative patients.

cards.t: Venous blood is what color?
cards.e: Venous blood is darker than arterial blood because it carries less oxygen.
qw: Bluish purple with a faint shine

cards.t: What is the body's first line of defense when a blood vessel is injured?
cards.d: The blood vessel constricts to reduce blood loss
w: The heart rate slows to reduce blood loss
Platelets and fibrin form a plug at the site of the injury
The blood vessel expands to allow clotting materials to flow out
cards.e: Vascular spasm narrows the injured vessel first. Platelet plugs come next.
cards.qd: The blood vessel constricts to reduce blood loss
qw: The heart rate slows to reduce blood loss
Platelets and fibrin form a plug at the site of the injury
The blood vessel expands to allow clotting materials to flow out

cards.t: Which term describes the complex series of events within the body related to blood clotting?
cards.e: The coagulation cascade is a chain of clotting factor reactions that forms a clot.

cards.t: What does blood plasma contain that blood serum does not?
cards.e: Serum is plasma without clotting proteins, so fibrinogen is found only in plasma.
qw: Red blood cells and their hemoglobin

cards.t: A specimen containing an anticoagulant additive and not spun in a centrifuge is called a(n) what specimen?
cards.e: A whole blood specimen keeps all blood components because the anticoagulant stops clotting.

cards.t: The buffy coat in a centrifuged specimen contains which cells?
cards.e: After centrifugation, the thin middle buffy coat holds white blood cells and platelets.
qw: White blood cells and plasma proteins
